- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in next 3–7 days; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model lags in adjusting; add 1–2 days of upward correction.
- Mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is >10% above recent 18d average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30d horizon, if true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% in 3+ consecutive days, model is underestimating trend; increase forecast by 1–2% per day.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating 0.33/1.00), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast with 3-day moving average.
